assessments.reasoning: The 1986 introduction explicitly treats SIMULA and SIMULA 67 as equivalent names within the standard and gives SIMULA I a separate historical role as an earlier language.

challenge.method: Can the equivalence absorb SIMULA I or resolve every unqualified historical use of SIMULA?
challenge.results: The predecessor designation rules out merging SIMULA I. The naming convention is expressly local to the standard. External uses need their own context, and active registry status remains an index classification.

limitations: The proposed identity is SIMULA 67. Ambiguous unqualified SIMULA usages outside this edition require contextual adjudication.
The active state is the index's proposed registry classification, independent of current upstream maintenance.
